transcript:
Meeting: Partner co-sell pipeline review with Helix Tech
Date/Time: 2026-06-24 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Morris (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Helix Head of Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (Helix Director Sales), Sofia Ruiz (Helix Solutions Architect)

Summary: Quick alignment on joint pipeline, discuss motion for three priority deals, ownership and escalation path, technical gating items (VPC / Dedicated / SOC2), and next steps for joint enablement and MDF/deal registration. Some transcription noise and mis-named product references (eg "Redwood Dediated"), filler words present.

Topics: pipeline review, co-sell motions, lead routing, deal registration, MDF and discounting, technical fit (hosted vs dedicated), benchmarks, security/compliance ask list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, we'll kick off, I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE on the account. Can everyone say hi?
[00:05] Maya: Hey Jordan, Maya here, thanks for setting up.
[00:07] Liam: Liam O'Connor, hi.
[00:09] Sofia: Sofia Ruiz, solutions.
[00:12] Priya: Priya Nair, SE at Redwood.
[00:14] Evan: Evan Morris, CSM, quick logistics notes after.
[00:18] Jordan: Great, goal for today is quick pipeline runthrough of the co-sell opps you shared, agree on who owns next steps, and flag any tech/security blockers. We'll aim 45-ish minutes and then action items.
[00:27] Maya: Sounds good. We shared a sheet with nine opportunities, but we highlighted three that are highest priority, two are in healthcare and one is in finserv.
[00:35] Priya: Perfect. Can we open with the first deal, "St. Rowan Health"? I see estimated ARR in the sheet. Can you confirm timeline?
[00:42] Liam: St. Rowan are in pilot now, they're budgeting Q3, exec sponsor wants production by Oct. They asked for an on-prem/private option early because of PHI.
[00:51] Sofia: yes, they asked specifically about VPC and ability to bring on-prem training data. They used the term "air-gapped" but it's mostly VPC + KMS.
[01:00] Priya: ok that maps to Redwood Private or our Dedicated offering. Quick note - Dedicated gives predictable throughput, but Private gives the KMS and network control customers often need for PHI. There's a cost delta.
[01:12] Jordan: For co-sell, Helix we expect you'll lead initial contact, we'll bring in SE support and a security brief. How do you want to route leads? Do you want direct handoff or intro via your partner portal?
[01:23] Maya: We prefer a warm intro from the Helix AE to the Redwood team, then joint discovery. Also for MDF and co-sell credit, we need a deal registration workflow.
[01:31] Evan: We have a partner deal registration template; Jordan will share. Typically MDF requests need expected ACV and a short plan.
[01:38] Liam: About pricing - are we able to offer a partner discount for the first year? Helps close in Q3.
[01:43] Jordan: We can discuss discount bands; for co-sells with Helix, Redwood standard is to reserve deeper discounts for registered deals with committed timelines. We'll draft example concessions and attach to the SOW.
[01:53] Maya: Are there any standard revenue splits or referral fees? Helix operates a revenue-share model usually.
[01:58] Jordan: We don't do a fixed split universally; we handle as part of MDF/partner compensation agreements. Evan will draft a proposed model for these three deals.
[02:07] Sofia: technical: for St. Rowan, primary ask is encryption at rest with customer KMS and audit logs for model invocations. Also SLAs for latency - they're concerned if we go hosted.
[02:18] Priya: latency and throughput profile will depend on model choice and sequence length. We'll propose a Dedicated pool with autoscale as a baseline, and show a hosted fallback. We'll run a benchmark with similar prompt sets.
[02:30] Jordan: Great, Priya you'll be running the benchmark. What's a realistic turnaround?
[02:34] Priya: If they share a prompt set and sample payloads today, I can run an initial latency/cost report in about one week. That will compare hosted vs dedicated vs private cost estimates.
[02:43] Maya: we'll send the prompt set and example data by Monday.
[02:46] Liam: on regulatory questions - St. Rowan's security team asked for SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit log retention details.
[02:55] Evan: Redwood has SOC 2 and ISO documentation, we support SAML/SSO, RBAC and audit logs. For Private deployments we can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC peering. I'll attach the security pack.
[03:07] Sofia: any notes about on-prem package? They asked if there's an air-gapped option for model weights.
[03:12] Priya: We have an on-prem package for regulated workloads but that often requires longer procurement and O&M from the customer. For many customers VPC + private control plane meets the needs without full air-gap.
[03:23] Jordan: moving to deal two: "Beacon Financial" (FinServ). Timeline is tighter, procurement is Nov/Dec. They're very price sensitive and care about latency for fraud models.
[03:34] Liam: Beacon is interesting, they've got existing GPU infra and love low latency. They asked if they should self-host or use Redwood Dedicated.
[03:42] Priya: If they already have infra, hybrid is an option - use Redwood Dedicated for peak and on-prem for base workload; or recommend Redwood Dedicated with guaranteed slots - usually cheaper ops for them. We'll show TCO.
[03:55] Jordan: Helix - will you lead the intro here or shall Redwood reach out?
[03:58] Liam: We'll set the intro, but Redwood should be ready for a deep technical session. They might ask for kernel-level perf numbers.
[04:06] Priya: ok we'll prep perf bench and also call out quantization profiles - that often saves cost without big quality loss.
[04:12] Maya: third deal is "Greenline Health" - small pilot, but high chance to scale. They want a short POC with a canary rollout.
[04:20] Jordan: For POC we usually do a 6-week pilot with defined success metrics. Who owns the POC scope?
[04:26] Maya: Helix will handle the initial integration and we'll do the data ingest. Redwood to provide the runtime hooks and monitoring.
[04:33] Evan: We'll provide per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns and a simple eval harness to monitor quality regressions. We'll also include rollbacks and canary policies.
[04:44] Sofia: regarding logs and PIIs, Greenline wants logs scrubbed. Is that doable?
[04:48] Priya: We can enable privacy masking and prefix/KV caching to reduce sensitive tokens in logs; we'll document limitations.
[04:55] Jordan: quick go-to-market ops: who at Helix is owning the joint pipeline in your CRM?
[05:00] Maya: Liam is the owner for healthcare deals, and I own partnerships ops. We'll export opportunities to you.
[05:06] Liam: for tracking we prefer a shared sheet and weekly sync cadence, is that acceptable?
[05:10] Jordan: yes weekly sync is fine, we'll make it 30 minutes. Evan will manage the calendar invite and JIRA for action items.
[05:18] Priya: technical gating: any account that needs PHI or other regulated data will probably need Private or on-prem; do we have any quick pricing ranges to share when Helix is discussing with their buyers?
[05:30] Jordan: I'll share an example pricing band for hosted vs dedicated vs private, but call out that private often needs an enterprise contract + onboarding fee.
[05:38] Sofia: our legal team also asked about indemnity and data residency terms. They want to see a sample SLA.
[05:45] Evan: I'll attach sample SLA and legal terms; legal will need to iterate but we can get a starting point.
[05:50] Liam: competitive landscape — Beacon mentioned they looked at Anthropic and Inferex for latency pricing. Any notes?
[05:57] Priya: Anthropic tends to be higher cost for low-latency configs, Inferex capabilities vary; we'll show benchmark comparisons but remind them that our orchestration and fallback policies are differentiators.
[06:09] Jordan: question for Helix — do you expect to co-brand the joint solution or keep Helix as primary reseller?
[06:14] Maya: Co-branding is good for leads we source together, but for some enterprise accounts we want Helix as primary with Redwood as underlying tech. We can decide per account.
[06:22] Jordan: ok flexibility is fine. On MDF: what budget cadence do you operate on?
[06:26] Maya: quarterly MDF requests, with approval leads two weeks. For close in Q3 we could get a quick approve if we provide ACV and use case.
[06:33] Evan: we'll propose a simple MDF request form Jordan will share.
[06:36] Priya: any security deep-dive requests? If so, we can schedule a technical security call with our compliance team.
[06:44] Sofia: St. Rowan's security lead wants a 60-minute session next week. Is that feasible?
[06:48] Jordan: Yes, Priya and Evan can join. Jordan to propose slots.
[06:52] Maya: parallel ask: Helix wants a co-sell enablement deck and a one-pager for Helix AEs on how to qualify Redwood deals.
[06:59] Evan: we'll create a one-pager and short playbook for sales motions.
[07:04] Jordan: let's talk skews - sorry, quotas - forgive me. For forecasting, Helix will provide weighted opps and Redwood will include them in the joint forecast; we need to agree on commit thresholds.
[07:16] Liam: we usually ask for 50% probability threshold to include in our commit forecast. Does that work?
[07:21] Jordan: yes, we'll accept that as a working rule.
[07:25] Maya: question: any limited-time incentives for Q3 closes?
[07:29] Jordan: we can consider limited promotional credits for first-month usage or pilot discounts if deals register and commit to timeline. We'll outline examples.
[07:36] Priya: technical follow-up: for the Beacon perf ask, do you have an example of kernel selection and batching improvements in the run time?
[07:44] Priya: (continues) Our runtime does continuous batching and KV cache management to reduce per-token cost; that is often a major lever. I might spell it "run time" in notes though, apologies.
[07:55] Liam: fair enough. Also they asked about model versioning and rollback during canary.
[07:59] Evan: Redwood supports model pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller variants if latency spikes. We'll demo that in the POC.
[08:09] Maya: anything on handoffs and support SLAs post-sale?
[08:13] Evan: for co-sell deals we'll include a support SLA in the SOW; for dedicated customers we offer a higher SLA and optional premium support.
[08:21] Jordan: ok time check - about 10 minutes left, let's capture final owners and dates.
[08:25] Jordan: Action items recap: Jordan to share deck and pricing bands by 2026-06-26; Priya to run perf bench by 2026-07-02; Evan to draft MDF/deal registration and sample SLA by 2026-07-06; Maya/Liam to share top 3 account contacts by 2026-06-29.
[08:44] Maya: noted. We'll also ask St. Rowan for a security slot next week.
[08:47] Jordan: Great, Evan will shoot out the calendar invites for weekly pipeline syncs.
[08:52] Liam: thanks everyone.
[08:54] Sofia: thanks, bye.
[08:56] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

References/Artifacts: joint pipeline spreadsheet (link in calendar note), partner deal registration template (link), security pack (link to docs).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-named terms ("Redwood Dedciated", "run time"), filler words, a few overlapping talk segments. Content includes typical negotiation points: discounts/MDF, technical gating for PHI (VPC/KMS), POC scope and exec intro.

End of transcript.
